title: Agent-driven setup and per-KB execution

nodes.summary: An agent installs Kyyn, checks readiness, opens KB for human
nodes.detail: The setup journey is agent-driven: an agent bootstraps/installs Kyyn, checks readiness, locates or creates a KB and launches its Web interface, explaining what was installed and what remains. No graphical installer or global daemon is a prerequisite.

realised.evidence: Only a developer install script (tools/install-cli.sh, PR #49) and kb init (PR #54) exist; no readiness check command or Web interface to launch

nodes.summary: Secrets set up per selected KB checkout, CLI-only
nodes.detail: Local secret setup targets the explicitly selected KB checkout's store (ADR 0016); an agent can help populate keys before sources/sinks run, values never travel through Git or come from another KB, and setup works from the CLI without Web or MCP.

realised.evidence: PR #122 adds checkout-local SecretStore with kyyn secret set/list/remove; Git-ignored values, no Web/MCP needed

nodes.summary: One-shot CLI commands with explicit KB selection, no server
nodes.detail: Ordinary CLI operations select a repository/KB explicitly, execute directly and exit with structured results and useful exit codes, requiring neither a Web server nor an MCP connection.

realised.evidence: PR #44 exposes the evolution journey through an optparse CLI with shared --kb PATH, human/JSON results and distinct exits

nodes.summary: Web and MCP are explicit on-demand per-KB processes
nodes.detail: A Web command starts a local server for one KB, reports its address and can open a browser; an MCP command serves one KB over stdio with an accurate client configuration example. Servers are explicit process choices started again on demand; leaving them running is not required KB state and stopping one need not stop the other.

realised.evidence: The CLI has no web, mcp or serve command at end of history; no server code in host/

nodes.summary: No global KB registry, session broker or in-memory owner
nodes.detail: Multiple processes may use the same repo and caches, sharing only persisted KB/workspace state; opening a KB is selection, not a canonical session object, and does not inject its tools into other agent sessions. ADR 0012's local-head rule covers concurrency; holding an immutable Validated Root is a snapshot, not ownership.

realised.evidence: Negative constraint; no code existed at seq 1 and no registry or session broker was ever built (each CLI call selects --kb)

nodes.summary: Lazy startup: cheap metadata operations never compile KB code
nodes.detail: Startup inspects identity/metadata without checking every root or compiling plugins; the first operation needing executable code may compile on a fresh clone and report progress/failure, while cheap operations such as listing drafts stay usable independently. Clients observe each other via persisted state; no collaborative editing or cross-process cancellation.

realised.evidence: PR #43 (seq 42) made EvolutionStore compiler-free; PR #44 ensures metadata-only commands neither read the SDK nor start MicroHs

nodes.summary: Closing keeps drafts and never claims to roll back effects
nodes.detail: Closing stops a server/connection or lets a one-shot command finish; drafts remain files, neither accepted nor deleted. Owned in-flight work is cancelled and resources released (ADRs 0007/0019), and once acceptance or external dispatch happened the actual outcome is reported rather than a rollback.

realised.evidence: Draft workspaces are ordinary files and the CLI reports publication/interruption outcomes honestly (PRs #42/#44); server shutdown is moot as no servers exist

nodes.summary: Automation is plain shell scripting; unready accept exits non-zero
nodes.detail: There is no Kyyn runner, scheduler, retry, task inbox or agent launcher: an external script creates a workspace, runs the user's own agent harness, then calls accept. Acceptance requires Ready plus a checked current candidate and matching base; otherwise it exits non-zero with a diagnostic, keeps the workspace, never marks Ready itself and never reruns acquisition.

realised.evidence: PR #44 provides evolution new/ready/accept with distinct outcome exits; acceptStoredEvolution refuses NotReady without changing the workspace

nodes.summary: Scripted accept composes with an explicit output-publish command
nodes.detail: After acceptance, the same script updates a declared output with ordinary typed renderer arguments via ADR 0017's preparation and explicit sink invocation, with no interactive preview; a failed acceptance stops a stop-on-error script before the sink runs, and uncertain sink outcomes are surfaced honestly.

realised.evidence: No output command group or sink invocation exists in the CLI at end of history

editorial.note: Delegates CLI navigation/KB selection to ADR 0018 and updates the illustrative script to pass the returned workspace ID and say 'output publish'; no change to what setup or automation requires
Metadata reconciliation only: frontmatter id/title, drops Status/Basis, renames 'Decision proposed' to 'Decision'

notes: Founding ADR with no ### subsections; 'Decision proposed' plus 'Automation is ordinary CLI scripting' were split into 9 commitments. 'First useful journey' was treated like Verification (a target end-to-end scenario spanning ADR 0021 slices 3-4) and produced no node. This lane never made a substantive decision after seq 1: its two later touches are editorial, so it is a fossil of the original product vision. That vision is half built: the CLI-shaped parts (one-shot commands with --kb, lazy compiler-free metadata ops, checkout-local secrets, scriptable accept with honest exits) were realised around seq 42-43 and 98, but everything server- or setup-shaped (agent bootstrap/readiness, per-KB Web and MCP processes, output publish in the automation script) is unrealised at end of history, so the ADR's headline 'agent installs Kyyn and opens the KB in a browser' journey remains white. 0025.05 (no registry/broker) is a negative constraint marked same_step only because nothing contrary was ever built; 0025.07 (closing) is low confidence since there are no servers to close.
